summary: Sporadic privileged API key usage observed after third-party webhook registration
summary_long: Automated webhook created by a third-party integration resulted in intermittent, unauthorised use of a privileged service API key tied to svc-webhook-consumer. Pattern appears correlated with external webhook registration events originating from a small set of foreign IPs.
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 we observed repeated spikes in privileged API calls originating from IPs not associated with our known vendors. Each spike followed a new webhook registration event for the same third-party integration name. Impact: Potential unauthorized use of a service account (svc-webhook-consumer) and elevated API activity that may expose data or state changes. Initial triage suggests the webhook registration flow allowed a callback URL that later triggered server-side token refresh behavior.
impact: Multiple high-privilege API calls (read/write) executed for short bursts over 3 distinct windows. No confirmed data exfiltration yet; potential risk to confidential customer metadata and internal job scheduling. Affects two regions' serving clusters; autoscaling also triggered additional GPU allocation during bursts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a new webhook integration via Console > Integrations > Add Integration using name 'thirdparty-webhook-ops'
2) Provide a callback URL hosted on a third-party domain and select 'svc-webhook-consumer' as the associated service account
3) Trigger a sample event from the third-party site and observe server-side token refresh and subsequent API calls in request logs
4) Confirm activity correlates to the time of registration in audit logs
logs: a) Request logs: multiple POST /v1/internal/jobs from svc-webhook-consumer token at 2026-03-12T09:21:13Z (ip=45.120.33.8)
b) Audit trail: integration.create events for integration id intg_98a7 at 2026-03-12T09:20:49Z by user automated-bot@example.com
c) Auth logs: token refresh events for svc-webhook-consumer at 2026-03-12T09:21:12Z and 2026-03-13T02:14:02Z
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The webhook registration flow inadvertently allowed third-party supplied metadata to influence token lifecycle behavior (callback URL triggered handshake causing server to refresh/retain token).
Observed IPs do not match any on our vendor allowlist; reverse lookup shows fastly-like provider hosting transient payload endpoints.
No obvious lateral movement detected from the service account; calls mainly invoke internal orchestration endpoints and a small set of read operations on customer metadata buckets.
SRE confirmed autoscaler reacted to higher request rate, creating temporary capacity in us-east which increased our cost footprint during bursts.
actions_taken: 1) Disabled new webhook registrations for 'thirdparty-webhook-ops' pattern and paused automated integration onboarding (2026-03-12 10:10Z)
2) Rotated svc-webhook-consumer API keys and revoked all active tokens for that service account (2026-03-12 10:45Z)
3) Blocklisted the observed IP ranges in the edge ACLs and added vendor allowlist checks (2026-03-12 11:05Z)
4) Deployed an emergency update to the registration service to validate callback domains against an allowlist and to avoid automatic long-lived token binding (2026-03-13 03:00Z)
5) Notified Product Security and Compliance; initiated targeted audit of recent webhook registrations (2026-03-12 12:00Z)
resolution: Mitigations applied (key rotation, webhook registration disabled, callback validation added). Ongoing: complete forensic review of affected service account activity and formal post-incident write-up. No customer-facing compromise confirmed; continue monitoring for recurring patterns.
next_steps: - Complete forensic timeline and expand log retention for integration.create and token.refresh events
- Run a tenant-scoped audit to flag any customer data read during the windows and notify affected owners if necessary
- Harden registration flow: require SSO-backed requester identity for privileged service bindings and limit default TTLs for service tokens
- Add automated alerting to detect registration -> token-refresh -> privileged-call sequences within 5 minutes
